margo: Quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC about a compact index for safetensors and the eager fallback path. Wanted to sync on edge cases and a small action plan.
ben: Compact index sounds great to cut metadata I/O, but main worry is partial-load detection — how do we avoid silent corruption when ranges are inconsistent?
akshay: One idea: per-shard tiny Bloom filter for chunk presence + a checksum per segment. Keeps index small but still lets runtime detect missing pieces cheaply.
lina: Bloom false positives could cause extra retries though. What false-positive rate are we comfortable with? 0.1%? 1%?
yusuf: Also need to consider compressed blobs (gz). Range reads on compressed files are awkward; fallback may need to fetch whole object. That changes the fallback cost model.
raf: Example range request we rely on:```curl -H "Range: bytes=102400-204799" https://weights.example/models/foo/part-0.safetensors``` If server doesn't support ranges, runtime should detect 206 vs 200 and switch modes.
ben: Good point. Compact index should include an explicit `supports_range` probe result cached per origin, so we don't keep guessing.
akshay: Also suggest exposing `index_version` and `segment_checksum` fields in the index schema. If checksum mismatch -> force full-validate path.
lina: API change for prefetcher: `get_shard_ranges(model, seq_len, fallback_budget_ms)` so callers can decide whether to stream or wait for index-based reads.
margo: Runtime heuristic proposal: estimate stream cost = latency_est + bytes_to_stream / network_throughput; if estimate < fallback_budget_ms -> stream eagerly, else try index-first. Metric name: `estimated_stream_ms`.
weights-bot: weights-indexer v2 pushed compact-index for model/foo@sha256:abc123 (index_version=1.1) :rocket:
yusuf: Note—when index is missing but we start streaming, we should concurrently kick off an async index build so future requests can use the index. Avoids repeated streaming costs.
raf: Tests we need: 1) origin doesn't support ranges -> ensure runtime falls back to full download and marks origin capability. 2) corrupt index checksum -> force full-validate and regenerate index. 3) partial-range served -> runtime retries with full fetch.
margo: Action items: akshay prototype Bloom + checksum layout (due in 48h), ben add `segment_checksum` + `index_version` to indexer, raf add tests for range/204/200/corrupt-index, lina update prefetch API and docs, yusuf prototype concurrent index-build-on-stream. I'll draft a short RFC patch with schema example.
ben: :+1: add a small note about quantized-shard mismatch — checksum must cover post-quantization bytes, not source weights.
akshay: Will do.
linA: tiny nit: prefer `fallback_budget_ms` default to 50ms for hosted low-latency tier, 200ms for dedicated.
margo: Good call. I'll include config defaults in the patch. Thanks all — back in 48h for updates.
